mechanism_narrative: Four consecutive weeks of narrowing TRANSIT and WORKPLACES deficits indicate a steady return of commuting and in-person work activity, which mechanically raises daytime foot traffic at retail and recreation venues over the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -32.1 to -6.7 over four weeks
fact:WORKPLACES improved from -34.4 to -23.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to improve week-on-week, indicating decoupling of commuting recovery from retail footfall.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen from 4.3 to 0.1 and is approaching zero, indicating households have nearly fully normalized time-at-home. Once RESIDENTIAL crosses below zero, the marginal behavioral driver of additional out-of-home retail trips disappears, causing RETAIL_REC growth to stall or reverse.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 0.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined monotonically from 4.3 to 0.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising at the same or faster rate for two or more weeks after RESIDENTIAL crosses below zero.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in PARKS and WORKPLACES reflects a broad-based lifting of restrictions across both leisure and work domains; when both series trend upward simultaneously, the combined effect reinforces household willingness to travel for retail, producing a larger positive move in RETAIL_REC than either series would predict alone.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -20.6 to 0.3 before the last week dip to -4.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is flat or negative despite both PARKS and WORKPLACES improving concurrently for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week deterioration in TRANSIT mobility typically signals newly imposed mobility restrictions or curfews; if such a policy shock occurs, retail and recreation visits will fall sharply within one to two weeks as access and incentive to travel for non-essential shopping is curtailed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has been improving but remains volatile with week-on-week swings up to 13 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline, or continues to rise, in the two weeks following a TRANSIT drop exceeding 15 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM growth has decelerated sharply from a 9.4-point weekly gain to a 0.6-point gain, suggesting essential-goods demand is saturating. Since GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC share the same underlying recovery-of-errands driver, this deceleration signals that the broader recovery impulse feeding RETAIL_REC is also exhausting, producing a near-term plateau or decline.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change falls below 1.0 point
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM weekly gains shrank from 10.7 to 9.4 to 0.6 points over the last three transitions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 points over the following week despite GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week growth falling below 1.0 point.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility reversed from 0.3 to -4.6 in the latest week, consistent with a seasonal shift away from outdoor leisure. This substitution effect redirects discretionary trips toward indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines for two consecutive weeks after a prior uptrend
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 0.3 to -4.6 in the most recent week after three weeks of gains
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS move in the same direction (both decline) over the next two weeks, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: The gap between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES deficits is narrowing (TRANSIT improved faster than WORKPLACES in recent weeks), indicating transit capacity is normalizing ahead of full workplace return. This excess transit capacity enables incremental non-commute trips, including retail visits, within the next week.
candidate_trigger: weekly improvement in TRANSIT exceeds weekly improvement in WORKPLACES by more than 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 4.4 points in the last week while WORKPLACES improved only 1.3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a period where TRANSIT improvement outpaces WORKPLACES improvement by more than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sustained improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT alongside declining RESIDENTIAL reflects a coordinated policy-driven reopening (eased restrictions on commuting and work). The joint signal of these three series moving together is a stronger predictor of retail recovery than any single series, driving a four-week rise in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES, TRANSIT improved and RESIDENTIAL declined concurrently across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue improving and RESIDENTIAL continues declining in tandem.
